prerequisites: Basic competencies in the use of programming languages and computer networks.
Ability to read and comprehend documentation written in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Know, select and use tools for collecting and organizing security data records.
Apply pattern and relationship detection techniques to security data records.
Manage tools for visualizing security attacks.
Design and implement offline and online security attack detection strategies.
Apply acquired theoretical-practical knowledge to use cases.

syllabus_topics: Collection, storage and organization of security data records
Analysis of attacks through the detection of characteristic patterns and interrelationships
Visualization of attacks from data records
Analysis and visualization strategies: offline and online
Handling of security records and data
Attack detection (scans, denial of service, malware, authentication)

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (P1) on Forensics laboratory sessions
Practical work (P2) on Network laboratory sessions
Practical work (P3) on Biometrics laboratory sessions

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum of 3 out of 10 must be achieved in each partial exam (T1, T2, T3) and each practical work (P1, P2, P3). If all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: 0.35 * (average of T1, T2, T3) + 0.5 * (average of P1, P2, P3) + 0.10 * active participation + 0.05 * attendance. If the minimums are not met, the continuous assessment grade will be 4.0, and the student must attend the ordinary call with a final exam and a single practical report. For ordinary, extraordinary, and differentiated evaluation calls, the final grade is calculated as: 0.5 * Theory exam + 0.5 * Practical work report.
